basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et ex illa dabo tibi filium cui benedicturus sum, eritque in nationes, et reges populorum'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et ex illa dabo tibi filium cui benedicturus sum, eritque in nationes, et reges populorum orientur ex eo. Signanterque non ut in Graeco legimus: dixit Deus ad Abraham, Sarai uxor tua non vocabitur Sarai; in Hebraeo habetur non vocabis nomen ejus Sarai; id est, non dices ei Princeps mea es: futura quippe omnium gentium jam princeps esse, unde et Apostolus Petrus mulierum vitam instituens ait: Sic enim aliquando et sanctae mulieres, sperantes in Domino, ornabant se subjectae propriis viris, sicut Sara obediebat Abrahae dominum eum vocans; cujus estis filiae benefacientes, et non perturbationem timentes ullam (I Petr. III, 5).
